entry.name: serial
entry.digest: Send and receive from a serial port

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: Specifies the serial port to be used by theobject. If alphabetic shortcuts (a-z) are used,specifies the first logical serial port in the computer, and-are used to specify additional ports.

arguments.name: portname
arguments.description: If actual portnames are used, the symbol is the name given by the Operating System to your port. Theto theobject can be used to create a list of available portnames and alphabetic shortcuts. If the port chosen is currently in use or unavailable when theobject is instantiated, an error message will be displayed and the object will not function. If no port is specified, the default port is.

arguments.name: rate
arguments.description: An optional argument may be used after the port name or alphabetic shortcut to specify the baud rate of the serial port (the default rate is 4800 baud). Any value is allowable (although not all ports can be set to all baud rates). Some common rates are 300, 600, 1200, 1800, 2400, 3600, 7200, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 and 115200.

arguments.name: data
arguments.description: After the baud rate, the next arguments specifies the number of data bits for the serial port (the default is 8 data bits). Other possible values are 5, 6 and 7.

arguments.name: stop
arguments.description: The next argument specifies the number of stop bits for the serial port. The default is 1. Other possible values are 1.5 (Windows only) and 2.

arguments.name: parity
arguments.description: The next argument specifies the parity for the serial port (the default is no parity, specified byor). Other possible values are(odd), and(even).

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: asyncread
attributes.digest: Read Continuously in Background
attributes.description: By default (= Off), the object only reads from the serial port when aarrives, or ifis enabled. When enabled (= On), reading is performed regularly in the background, and amessage (or polling) will cause the asynchronously read bytes to be output.

attributes.name: autoopen
attributes.digest: Auto-open flag
attributes.description: Toggles automatically opening the serial port.

attributes.digest: Baud rate

attributes.name: break_duration
attributes.digest: Break Duration (microseconds)
attributes.description: Specifies the duration of a break signal in microseconds (the default duration is 1ms, or 1000us). Some applications, such as DMX, require break durations in a particular range when marking frames.

attributes.name: bufsize
attributes.digest: Input buffer size
attributes.description: Sets the input buffer size used by theobject. The default buffer size is 2048.

attributes.name: chunk
attributes.digest: Data list length
attributes.description: Sets the data chunk size (data list length) for output.

attributes.description: Sets the number of data bits (acceptable values are,,, or).

attributes.name: defer
attributes.digest: Defer output
attributes.description: Defer output of messages to the lower priority main thread. Most applicable when using Overdrive.

attributes.name: drain
attributes.digest: Drain enable flag
attributes.description: (Mac only) Toggles drain enable. When enabled, communication waits until all data has been transmitted to the terminal when writing. The default value is 0 (disabled).

attributes.name: dtr
attributes.digest: DTR (data terminal ready) enable
attributes.description: Enables or disables the DTR (data terminal ready) function of the serial port used by theobject.

choices.digest: Use the connection default (do not change)

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Sends each character received on the serial port since the lastmessage out theobject's left outlet as an integer in the order that the characters were received. Before output data is sent, the message, followed by a number specifying the number of bytes received is sent out the right outlet of theobject.

messages.name: break
messages.description: Sends a break command to the serial port used by theobject. After the break has completed, the messageis sent out the object's right outlet.

messages.name: close
messages.description: Closes an open serial connection, permitting use of the serial port by other applications.

messages.name: getport
messages.description: Sends the name or shortcut of the currently open serial port out theobject's right outlet, prepended by the word.

messages.name: int
messages.description: Sends the number out the serial port accessed by theobject. Numbers outside the range 0-255 are wrapped to that range using a modulo operator. After the data is sent, the message, followed by a number specifying the number of bytes sent is sent out the right outlet of theobject.

messages.name: list
messages.description: Sends each number in the list out the serial port, in order. Numbers outside the range 0-255 are wrapped to that range using a modulo operator. After the data is sent, the message, followed by a number specifying the number of bytes sent is sent out the right outlet of theobject.

messages.name: port
messages.description: The word port, followed by a symbol, specifies the serial port to be used by the object. If alphabetic shortcuts are used, a specifies the first logical serial port in the computer. b - z specify additional ports. If actual portnames are used, the symbol is the name given by the operating system to your port. See themessage for a way to list available portnames and alphabetic shortcuts. If the port chosen is currently in use or unavailable when the port message is sent, an error message will be displayed and the object will revert to its previously chosen port, or won't function if there was none.

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Print a list of serial ports
messages.description: Sends a list of available serial ports to the Max Console, along with their alphabetic shortcuts. The message... is also sent from the object's right outlet, with a list of available ports.

messages.name: refresh
messages.description: Refreshes the list of known/available serial ports. See themessage for additional information.

messages.name: reset
messages.digest: Reset the serial port for Basic Stamp
messages.description: (Mac only) Resets the currently open serial port using the Basic Stamp initialization sequence.
